prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external-processing; delivers predictable-latency, quality-documented imagery. Mission Control Center (Bluebell: local-voice-only) owns authorization/readiness/schedules/routing; coordinates instrument-mode/downlink-priority/reception-gap impacts with Payload Processing Facility; sends anomaly/outage/configuration constraints to Mission Planning System; records unresolved-actions/questions/expected-specialist-responses each shift. Escalation: console lead→discipline lead→mission management for safety/contact-continuity/recovery threats. Specialists must be reachable for critical/off-nominal activities; suspected onboard faults require preserved command-state, no discretionary commands, specialist review before reconfiguration. Mission Planning System (Cedar), authoritative candidate-observation/contact planner, receives requests via User Services Portal/Mission Control Center; screens authority/target/urgency/acquisition-mode/volume/restrictions; combines priorities/instrument-availability/contacts/storage/downlink into drafts. Planning/release segregated; Command Validation Gateway must validate uplinks. User Services Portal records acceptance versus technical-review states; provides search/orders/status/support. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral: legacy-shift-logs) supplies orbit/maneuver/navigation/visibility/pointing, including planning predictions/assumptions. Orbit Determination Engine consumes tracking, produces controlled orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report. Spacecraft Operations Team owns safety/contact-decisions, monitors spacecraft health, reviews late attitude/thermal/command-capacity/contact requests; coordinates command-timing/attitude/tracking/post-burn assessment with Flight Dynamics Team, which separates clock-bias/tracking-error. Telemetry Ingest Service receives frames/contact-status/flow-indicators; validates framing/time-continuity, records reception metadata/interruption distinctions; supplies operations/engineering/processing and Pass Replay Packet. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse: consoles/shift-logs) coordinates processing/calibration/quality/distribution. Payload Calibration Team owns performance/quality; sends approved Calibration Patch Bundle. Primary Processing Cluster nominal; Backup Processing Cluster controlled-failover/lower-preference, firewall/return-paths routinely tested. Long Term Archive preserves data/products/evidence; contact-rate-limited transfers protect telemetry/control. Product Quality Service checks dissemination. Network Control System (Lantern) owns circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact-records; sends antenna-status/link-configuration/timing-references/routing-readiness to Mission Control Center prepass. Ground Network Manager (Juniper: standing-rosters) owns

New part:
S108: The draft schedule covers payload imaging, recorder management, housekeeping activities, and expected support from the North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna.
S109: For high-volume acquisitions, the schedule also accounts for downlink opportunities through the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna.
S110: The Payload Processing Facility receives planning metadata needed to prepare downstream processing expectations without treating the planning schedule as a commitment to deliver products.
S111: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are considered during planning only to verify that expected acquisition loads remain compatible with routine processing capacity.
S112: Juniper confirms that planned station use is compatible with network maintenance windows before the schedule is released for command preparation.
S113: The Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Antenna Deicing Notice to assess whether planned support can proceed without adding contingency contact margin.
S114: The Mission Planning System flags conflicts when two activities compete for the same spacecraft resource, ground station resource, or operational staffing interval.
S115: Constraint checking includes slew time, sun-angle limits, power balance, thermal recovery time, recorder capacity, command load size, and required separation between incompatible activities.
S116: The Flight Dynamics Team reviews cases where orbital uncertainty or contact geometry could reduce the execution margin for a planned acquisition or downlink.
S117: The Payload Calibration Team reviews planned calibration activities when they share resources with revenue observations or affect instrument configuration states.
S118: After schedule convergence, the Mission Planning System exports a command preparation package to the command engineering workflow at the Mission Control Center.
S119: The Command Validation Gateway, also called Osprey in this section, performs independent validation of command stacks before they are eligible for operational approval.
S120: Command stack validation checks syntax, timing, parameter ranges, sequencing rules, spacecraft mode compatibility, and consistency with the approved schedule baseline.
S121: The Command Validation Gateway rejects command stacks that contain unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired configuration references, or activities outside the planning authority window.
S122: The Telemetry Ingest Service is consulted for the latest spacecraft state needed to confirm that the command assumptions still match actual configuration and health.
S123: The Orbit Determination Engine provides the current orbital solution used to confirm time-tagged events, contact visibility, and any attitude-dependent observation geometry.
S124: The Product Quality Service may add planning feedback when previous acquisitions indicate that a requested geometry or instrument mode is unlikely to meet quality objectives.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
